episodes.180613: During the afternoon hours of July 13th a lone storm along a quasi-stationary frontal boundary produced large hail across portions of Jennings county.
episodes.180641: Scattered thunderstorms occurred across the region, one of which produced small hail.
episodes.180674: Widely scattered showers and storms developed ahead of a cold front as it approached central Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening of July 13, 2023. The storms produced sporadic wind damage and one report of quarter-sized hail.
episodes.180685: High pressure centered over eastern Arizona and New Mexico brought seasonal moisture into eastern sections of Arizona. Some showers and thunderstorms developed that produced locally heavy rain.
episodes.180686: A severe thunderstorm developed in Scotts Bluff County and moved southeast into Morrill County the evening of 12 July 2023.
episodes.180687: Severe thunderstorms developed across most counties in the Nebraska Panhandle 13 July 2023.
episodes.180758: Higher low-level moisture on July 13th and a backdoor cold front replenishing this moisture for July 14th and 15th combined with robust upper level wind shear produced three days of severe weather across eastern NM. Severe weather impacts were limited to northeastern NM on the 13th and 14th, becoming more widespread across northeastern and east-central NM on the 15th. There were a few thunderstorm wind gusts measured in the vicinity of the White Sands Missile Range on the 13th and 14th, likely from dry microbursts as the exception for the 13th and 14th. More substantial reports of damage and large hail occurred on the 15th ranging from broken skylights, flooding, accumulated hail, and a tornado. Thankfully, there were no reports of injuries or casualties.
episodes.181192: A few thunderstorms developed during the evening hours over northeast Montana, with a couple reaching severe levels.
episodes.181220: Showers and thunderstorms developed in West Virginia on the afternoons of July 13th through 15th in the midst of weak disturbances passing through the area.  Strong wind gusts accompanying storms resulted in multiple downed trees across the state. Flash flooding also blocked sections of a road in Raleigh County on the 13th while another isolated instance of flash flooding occurred on the 15th in Clay County. Storms tapered down with the loss of daytime heating after sunset each evening.
episodes.181225: Showers and thunderstorms developed in eastern Kentucky on the afternoon of July 13th in the midst of weak disturbances passing through the area. Abundant moisture was in place during this time with surface dew points above 70 degrees, which allowed storms to thrive during the daylight hours. Strong wind gusts accompanying storms resulted in downed trees around Greenup, one of which fell onto a local home. Storms tapered down with the loss of daytime heating after sunset.
episodes.181226: Areas of showers and thunderstorms developed on the afternoon of July 13th in southeast Ohio as a result of a nearby disturbance. A few thunderstorms materialized that day and reached strong to severe levels, causing damaging wind gusts and downed trees as a result. Lawrence and Gallia Counties saw the brunt of stronger storms that afternoon, with a few trees causing traffic obstructions as they laid onto the roadways.
episodes.181424: An isolated severe thunderstorm moved slowly east across the Ozark foothills. The storm occurred along a weak frontal boundary that was draped from the Ohio Valley southwest across the Ozarks.
episodes.181601: A cold front crossing the region along with building instability resulted in a line of severe thunderstorms sweeping east from the Genesee valley and northern Finger Lakes on into the North Country during the afternoon. Numerous reports of wind damage were received.
episodes.181661: A strong thunderstorm tracked across southern portions of Ziebach County, producing hail to around penny size and gusty winds.
episodes.181662: A supercell thunderstorm tracked southeast across portions of Oglala Lakota County, producing large hail and wind gusts over 80 mph. The combination of strong winds and hail caused considerable damage along its path.
episodes.181779: There were numerous reports of damaging wind gusts as a result of severe storms on July 12th.
episodes.182092: An upper level wave moved across northern and eastern Iowa. By peak afternoon heating, thunderstorms began developing along the boundary in northeast Iowa into southern Minnesota.  DCAPE approached 900 J/kg, supporting gusty winds with storms that developed. At the same time, deep layer shear over 40 knots and steep lapse rates supported hail growth, with several reports of quarter sized hail as the storms moved southeast.
episodes.182170: Despite an upper ridge extending from the Desert Southwest into the Southern Plains, scattered diurnal storms developed during the evening of the 13th. While weak magnitudes of organizing wind shear existed across the area, storm organization occurred along the composite outflow from initial storms across western-north Texas into southwestern Oklahoma. Damaging downburst wind events and a few reports of large hail were received with the strongest storms.
episodes.182171: Despite an upper ridge extending from the Desert Southwest into the Southern Plains, scattered diurnal storms developed during the evening of the 13th. While weak magnitudes of organizing wind shear existed across the area, storm organization occurred along the composite outflow from initial storms across western-north Texas into southwestern Oklahoma. Damaging downburst wind events and a few reports of large hail were received with the strongest storms.
episodes.182324: Storms developed over southeast Kansas ahead of an approaching cold front during the evening of the 12th and moved across far southeastern Kansas through the morning of the 13th. Sporadic wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph downed trees and power poles from Arcadia and Fort Scott in Kansas. Flash flooding was reported in Pittsburg, Kansas where water rescues and stranded vehicles were reported.
episodes.182338: Isolated thunderstorms developed along a weak frontal boundary that was draped along the Ohio River.
episodes.182513: Scattered thunderstorms, some with torrential rainfall affected portions of Addison and Rutland Counties. One to locally four inches of rain fell in a some areas, leading to a few reports of flash flooding and road washouts.
episodes.182618: A cold front passed through Central New York, triggering scattered showers and thunderstorms. An unstable environment supported multiple severe thunderstorms that contained damaging wind gusts and large hail. Most of the storm reports were for downed trees and wires.
episodes.182619: A cold front passed through Northeastern Pennsylvania, triggering scattered showers and thunderstorms. An unstable environment supported multiple severe thunderstorms that contained damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.182743: A tornado damaged a storage facility on the east side of Colon and then caused sporadic damage to trees along its 2.92 mile track.
episodes.182918: Thunderstorms developed along a dryline and brought severe weather across central to northeastern South Dakota during the mid-afternoon hours. Large hail, between quarter and golf ball size, was the main threat, along with isolated severe wind gusts. Hail nearly covered the ground near Fort Sisseton. Hail also covered the ground, up to three inches deep in some spots, six miles east of Carpenter. Penny to quarter-size hail and 55 mph wind gusts were reported eight miles east-southeast of Rosseau. Tree branches, 4 inches in diameter, were downed.
episodes.183033: Severe storms survived from the Devils Lake Basin down into Lakes Country Minnesota. These storms dropped severe hail, and damaging wind gusts throughout the region.
episodes.183035: Severe storms survived from the Devils Lake Basin down into Lakes Country Minnesota. These storms dropped severe hail and damaging wind gusts throughout the region.
episodes.183083: Thunderstorms developed over eastern Kansas during the evening of the 12th, along a cold front as a weak upper level disturbance approached the Southern and Central Plains. The storms moved southeast across northwestern Arkansas during the early morning hours of the 13th, the strongest of which produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.183168: Shortwave troughs crossing the region, and cooler temperatures aloft, led to the ideal environment for an active afternoon and evening on July 13th with widespread showers and thunderstorms. Ample diurnal heating increased instability across the region which led to numerous thunderstorms with the primary hazard of damaging winds.
episodes.183288: Two groups of supercells moved out of South Dakota and into northern Nebraska during the afternoon and early evening, with the second eventually converging into a small squall line. Another cluster of supercells moved from the panhandle into southwest Nebraska and also evolved into a squall line. Several reports of large hail and damaging winds were received, primarily in Cherry County and a swath from Garden to Lincoln counties.
episodes.183340: Scattered strong to severe storms during the afternoon and evening of July 14th impacted the Northern Plains into the Upper Mississippi River Valley. The primary threat was hail with penny sized reported near Stacyville (Mitchell County) and quarter sized hail reported near New Hampton (Fayette County).
episodes.183356: A slowly southward-moving front was draped across central Ohio and Pennsylvania on July 13th.  Warm air aloft initially kept storm development muted, but a mesoscaled convective vortex fired thunderstorms by early to mid-afternoon over the Middle Ohio Valley.  These storms lifted northeastward into an environment characterized by 40 to 50 knots of deep-layer shear and up to 2500 J/kg of mixed layer CAPE.  Dry air aloft also enhanced the downburst wind threat.  As a result, many reports of tree damage were received across southwest Pennsylvania, along with several instances of marginally severe hail.
episodes.183357: A slowly southward-moving front was draped across central Ohio and Pennsylvania on July 13th.  Warm air aloft initially kept storm development muted, but a mesoscale convective vortex fired thunderstorms by early to mid-afternoon over the Middle Ohio Valley.  These storms lifted northeastward into an environment characterized by 40 to 50 knots of deep-layer shear and up to 2500 J/kg of mixed layer CAPE.  Dry air aloft also enhanced the downburst wind threat. A few reports of severe wind were received.
episodes.183358: A slowly southward-moving front was draped across central Ohio and Pennsylvania on July 13th.  Warm air aloft initially kept storm development muted, but a mesoscaled convective vortex fired thunderstorms by early to mid-afternoon over the Middle Ohio Valley.  These storms lifted northeastward into an environment characterized by 40 to 50 knots of deep-layer shear and up to 2500 J/kg of mixed layer CAPE.  Dry air aloft also enhanced the downburst wind threat.  As a result, a few reports of wind damage were received from Marshall and Ohio Counties.
episodes.183408: During the afternoon of July 13th, a cluster of thunderstorms developed in East-Central Colorado and moved south-southeastward across the region. One of these thunderstorms became severe and produced hail up to baseballs in size within the region.
episodes.183414: A moist and unstable airmass was present over southwest Alabama during the morning hours with PWATs near 2.5 inches. Slow moving thunderstorms developed during the early morning hours over Sumter County.  Significant flooding occurred with radar estimated rainfall amounts of 6 to 8 inches fell over a three hour period. Additional storms developed on July 14th and produced localized flooding in Shelby County.
episodes.183425: A couple of isolated severe storms moved across the southern Texas Panhandle during the late afternoon/early evening hours of the 13th. One of which produced hail 1.25 in diameter. As the evening progressed these storms moved west to east merging with a line of storms from the Texas Panhandle and ran south through much of West Texas. Also a couple of initial supercells entered the northwestern combined Panhandles producing hail up to 1.25 in diameter as well. A complex eventually formed in southeast Colorado and moved southeast into the combined Panhandles becoming the main focus for severe storms going into the early AM hours of the 14th. Severe wind gusts became the main threat with winds reaching up to 75 mph measured, and 85 mph estimated from wind damage.
episodes.183438: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms ahead and along a cold frontal boundary resulted in widespread downed trees and wires and a few reports of flooding across eastern New York during the afternoon and evening hours of July 13, 2023. One injury was reported as a tree fell onto an occupied vehicle. Thousands were left without power across the Capital Region.||Additional isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed during the evening and early overnight hours on July 14-15, 2023 producing additional reports of hail, wind damage and flooding.
episodes.183514: Isolated showers and storms were seen throughout the area, with a few reports of small hail and gusty winds. One report of severe hail was received in Van Horne, Iowa.
episodes.183532: Storms developed over central Missouri and southeast Kansas ahead of an approaching cold front during the evening of the 12th and moved across southwest and south central Missouri through the early morning of the 13th. Sporadic wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph downed trees and power poles from Arcadia and Fort Scott in Kansas eastward to near Joplin, Billings, Marshfield, and Cabool. Widespread rainfall accumulations over an inch occurred across the entire region, with a band of two to five inches extending along and north of a line from Pittsburg, Kansas to Bolivar to Salem. Flash flooding was reported in Pittsburg, Kansas where water rescues and stranded vehicles were reported. Flash flooding also occurred near Couch in Oregon County when Townfork Creek rose rapidly out of its banks.
episodes.183533: Storms developed over eastern Oklahoma and southeast Kansas during the evening of the 13th and moved along the Missouri and Arkansas border during the early morning of the 14th. The strongest storms produced up to ping-pong ball sized hail over Oregon County. Rainfall accumulations ranged from one to two inches near the Missouri and Arkansas Border.  A second round of storms developed over central Nebraska during the morning of the 14th and moved southeastward across eastern Kansas and into the  Missouri Ozarks through the evening of the 14th. These storms produced a swath of wind gusts over 60 mph from Fort Scott, Kansas to Branson, and led to widespread tree and powerline damage. Rainfall amounts averaged between one-half inch and one inch along and west of a line from Nevada to Gainesville.
episodes.183541: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms ahead and along a cold frontal boundary resulted in widespread downed trees and wires across western Massachusetts during the afternoon and evening hours of July 13, 2023.
episodes.183542: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms ahead and along a cold frontal boundary resulted in widespread downed trees and wires across southern Vermont during the afternoon and evening hours of July 13, 2023.
episodes.183597: A slow-moving cold front dropping south from the Ohio Valley. As this front encountered an airmass with modest shear and very unstable conditions, it allowed allowed for afternoon thunderstorms to develop. Some of these storms were discrete and produced large hail. After the storms began to merge into bowing segments, damaging winds resulted.
episodes.183598: A slow-moving cold front dropping south from the Ohio Valley. As this front encountered an airmass with modest shear and very unstable conditions, it allowed allowed for afternoon thunderstorms to develop. Some of these storms produced damaging winds in western Greenbrier county.
episodes.183720: During the late night hours of July 12th, a weak boundary sagged into southeast Kansas which helped to trigger strong to severe thunderstorms across that area. Severe winds around 60 to 65 mph and very heavy rainfall which caused flooding in some areas.
episodes.183777: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail and damage winds across parts of Lincoln, Washington and Weld counties.  Significant crop damage was observed northwest of Stoneham in northeast Weld County.  In addition, the combination of hail and wind damaged trees and property.  The hail ranged in size from 1 to 3.25 inches in diameter, with peak wind gusts estimated up to 70 mph.  One brief tornado touched down in Lincoln County, but no damage was observed.
episodes.183808: Another in a series of jet streaks in northwest flow aloft initiated afternoon and early evening convection across eastern South Dakota, southwest Minnesota, and northwest Iowa.  Several storms in an environment of 1500-2000 MLCAPE and around 40 knots of distributed deep-layer shear took on supercellular characteristics and produced hail up to baseball size in southwest Minnesota.
episodes.183817: Another in a series of jet streaks in northwest flow aloft initiated afternoon and early evening convection across eastern South Dakota, southwest Minnesota, and northwest Iowa. Several storms in an environment of 1500-2000 MLCAPE and around 40 knots of distributed deep-layer shear took on supercellular characteristics and produced hail up to baseball size in southwest Minnesota.
episodes.183926: A slow-moving cold front dropping south from the Ohio Valley. As this front encountered an airmass with modest shear and very unstable conditions, it allowed allowed for afternoon thunderstorms to develop. A bowing line of storms produced damaging winds across Surry County.
episodes.183956: Numerous waterspouts developed in association with developing showers along a regenerative convective cloud line flanking the Lower Florida Keys. The atmosphere consisted of high convective available energy and little if any convective inhibition.
episodes.184029: Upper level low pressure was centered over Hudson Bay to start the day on the 13th, with generally zonal west to east flow from the central Plains through the Mid-Atlantic.  A slow-moving cold front was draped across the Ohio River Valley.  Early in the day, an upper level disturbance embedded in the upper level windflow was observed crossing southern Ohio and West Virginia, reaching central Virginia during the afternoon.  Thunderstorm activity increased in an environment of surface-based CAPEs climbing to around 3,000 J/Kg, while precipitable water values climbed into the 1.7 to 1.9 inch range by early evening.  A series of thunderstorms passed across the City of Lynchburg and northern Campbell County during the evening, producing 3 to locally 6 inch per hour rainfall rates.  The first storm passed across Lynchburg shortly after 4 pm, with additional rounds arriving at 6 pm, 7 pm and 9 pm.  Each round brought 1 to 3 inches of rain to the city, depending on location.  CREST Unit Streamflows rising over 1,000 cfs per mi^2.  FLASH Average Recurrence Intervals maxed out at over a 200-year rainfall event at the 6-hour duration.
episodes.184072: A mid level disturbance combined with a surface front and weak wave of low pressure moved across an unstable air mass over northern New York during the afternoon of July 13th. Several lines of showers and thunderstorms moved across the region with some storms producing damaging winds.
episodes.184076: A mid level disturbance combined with a surface front and weak wave of low pressure moved across an unstable air mass over Vermont during the afternoon and evening of July 13th. Several lines of showers and thunderstorms moved across the region with some storms producing damaging winds, including a microburst and a weak tornado.
episodes.184129: The continuations of hail, wind, and tornadoes continues through mid-July as northwesterly upper level flow develops once again over southern Colorado. Anomalous amounts of low level moisture remain over the region due to record breaking precipitation in June and an active early July. Enhanced wind shear due from the upper level northwesterly flow created an environment conducive to severe thunderstorms.
episodes.184172: Several scattered thunderstorms developed in northwest flow and moved across the region. These storms has supercell characteristics, and were efficient hail producers. There were several reports of golfball size or larger hail.
episodes.184189: During the evening of July 12, scattered thunderstorms dropped 13 tornadoes across far northeast Illinois, primarily within the west of northwest suburbs of Chicago. Of these 13 tornadoes, three were determined to be EF-1 with the remaining 10 being EF-0.
episodes.184198: A video shared via Twitter showed a waterspout over Lake Michigan east of North Avenue Beach.
episodes.184288: Thunderstorms developed along an old outflow boundary across parts of central and east central Missouri. Some of the storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.184350: A strong system moved through Eastern Washington and brought scattered thunderstorms. The main areas stretched along Highway 2 from Waterville Plateau to Northern Spokane County.
episodes.185416: A significant flash flood event unfolded during the early morning hours of July 13th into the late morning and midday. A corridor of 6 to 9 inches fell, with locally higher amounts, roughly from Ackerman to Louisville to DeKalb MS. Some of the most impacted areas were across Choctaw and Winston Counties. Multiple roads were flooded, washed out or closed. Many structures were flooded as well along with stalled or submerged vehicles.

After the first tornado in the O'Hare area lifted, a second EF-0 tornado touched down within the confines of O'Hare Airport just south of the I-90 overpass over Touhy Ave. The tornado initially caused minor roofing and fascia damage to buildings and warehouses on the far north side of the airport. Minor tree damage also occurred in this area, and a parked car was impaled by debris that was thrown by the tornado. The tornado then tracked east across I-90 and into Rosemont, where it blew over a light pole and ticket booths in the Allstate Arena parking lot and caused damage to trees and signs along Mannheim Rd. Video footage taken in Rosemont showed the tornado (which did not necessarily have a fully condensed cloud-to-ground funnel at all times) track into a residential area on the southeast side of Des Plaines, where it produced a concentrated area of tree damage, caused minor roofing and fascia damage to some houses, and caused a few power poles to lean. The tornado may have lost contact with the ground as it crossed the Des Plaines River, but it eventually touched down again in Park Ridge, where it produced tree damage in a neighborhood east of Maine South High School before lifting for good.

A tornado quickly developed almost directly over a storage facility on the east side of Colon in St. Joseph county. Garage doors were blown in and then a significant loss of roof decking and metal covering occurred. This wood and metal debris was lofted, twisted, and deposited both to the east and north up to 200 yards away in nearby fields. The tornado crossed into Branch county with sporadic tree damage noted on Ambs Road, South Culver Road, and Jackson Road, where large branches were down, trees uprooted, or trees were snapped several feet off the ground. The tornado topped a number of trees within a tree grove east of Jackson Road, but south of Wattles |Road before dissipating. The tornado was on the ground for 0.9 miles in St Joseph county and 2.0 miles in Branch county for a total of 2.9 miles in length.

Water entered homes and businesses including residences near Mount Moriah Street, a community center along Church Street, and a retail store along MS highway 14 on the east side of Louisville. Runoff from up to 6 inches of rainfall resulted in over one foot of flowing water along Fort Avenue. Several cars were inundated up to their windows by the flooding, with water entering the passenger compartments.  The road was closed until flooding receded.  No damage was reported to the road.

Heavy rainfall was widespread across the City of Lynchburg, with rates observed as high as 5 inches per hour at times.  The rainfall overwhelmed storm water drains, causing heavy runoff to flow down roads and across properties within the city.  Flash flooding occurred on several roads within the city, causing them to be impassible until the flooding receded.  These roads include the 2500 block of Carroll Avenue, Old Campbell Avenue, Otey Street, Oakley Avenue at Wythe Road, Kemper Street, McConville Road.
